I'm heartbroken. The Mass Effect trilogy is one of the best sci-fi, heck one the best stories and games of all time. It's fun to play, it's rich in lore and depth of the universe and there are multiple really interesting story lines and philosophical concepts.

But why am I heartbroken? *Mild spoiler*
Because of that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending. I won't spoil the endings, but I will rant about them. That was one of the worst endings I've witnessed. Sure, there are plenty of actually worse endings to stories. But due to how amazing the Mass Effect games are, this ending felt so much. "It's just a game" You might say. But no, some games, like these ones, are an experience. But this experience ended so terribly that I was actually upset after completing it. The ending was an insult to Mass Effect and the players who paid to play them. The extended cuts to "fix" the endings doesn't fix them at all, they're still all terrible. So I've chosen to ignore the endings and I've made up two alternative endings in my mind. Gosh, how the ♥♥♥♥ could they screw up the endings that badly considering the material they had written up to that point? I can argue why I think the endings are terrible, but I'll not do so here as to avoid spoilers. But in short I could summarize it as: They ignored and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the thematic tone they had set throughout the games and you could say the endings were generic in a fashion and the games deserved something better than that.

So would I recommend it? If you can overlook a terrible ending and is creative enough to think up more suitable endings, then yes, I would still recommend playing the trilogy because of everything up until the climax is really awesome if you like epic sci-fi.

I wish there was a middle recommendation button "maybe" or something, but I'll click the "Yes" button.

Also I should probably recommend getting the new version of the trilogy, the legendary or whatever it's called, rather than this version.

First of all, it says 6.7 hours, but i stopped playing and then bought the legendary edition for the PS5 and then spent 92 hours playing this series non-stop. I feel compelled to review the third game specifically because of how this game in particular spoke to me. I tried to play this game twice before I finally bit the bullet and finished it. Once when I was 15, and again last year, and now finally I 100%ed it. I played Mass Effect 1 and 2 three times over before I finally finished ME 3. I can say with all honesty, that Mass Effect 3 is one of the finest video games I have every played. It is easily my favorite of the trilogy and I will explain why despite its more than lackluster ending. 

Mass Effect as a trilogy was built around the impending doom of the Reaper invasion and the group of heroes led by Commander Shepherd to stop them. Mass Effect 1 introduced us the these band of heroes, Mass Effect 2 added more characters and fleshed out the ones we loved and made us care for the new ones as well. Mass Effect 3 takes the time spent developing those characters and making us love them and then uses that care to develop a story that is literally perfect (Up until the final 15 minutes of this game). The scenarios and character/story arcs that develop throughout this game in particular are some of the most thrilling and well written pieces of media let alone video games that I've ever had the privilege to experience. Multiple parts of this game had me holding back tears as the game takes characters we've spent years getting to know go through hell to fight off what seems like an unwinnable enemy. By the time I finished the Citadel DLC and I had to continue the story to end the game, I didn't want the game to end. I would have done anything to get one more second in this game with these characters as my commander shepherd. Few games have garnered such emotion from me. 

This game was so good to me that it begged the question from me. If I had 91.75 great hours in this series, does that oh so sour final 15 minutes destroy what I had come to love. To be honest, I don't have an answer. I think that I will never forget my time with this series, and this entry in particular is one I hope to remember quiet fondly. I think with a game like this, and with characters this strong, Mass Effect as a series was never about the destination. It was about the Journey with these characters and the adventures you had with them. 

I can comfortably say that if you believe that a quarter of an hour can sour your almost 100 hours spent playing through this series than probably wait to see if Mass Effect 4 will be any good. If you can look past was is probably one of the worst endings to anything I've ever experienced then please do play this game, because that journey is one you won't soon forget. 

So long Commander

The finale to the greatest sci-fi trilogy of all time. Bar none. This game brings all of the decisions made in the previous instalments to fruition, even in the ending. Ignore the tired memes, Mass Effect 3's amazing ending has been fixed with patches and DLC for over half a decade. The gameplay is a combination of action shooter, blended with classic RPG elements to make a wonderful blend of depth without complicating things. The great voice acting from the previous instalments continues to shine here, Ali Hillis (Dr. Liara T'Soni) and Keith David (Admiral David Anderson) deliver virtuoso performances.

While the Legendary Edition is the one to get (it supports 21:9, while this original version does not), the original iteration of Mass Effect 3 is the only way to play ME3's cooperative multiplayer mode, a fun, light mode that expands the scope of the war with the Reapers.
Would only buy this for the multiplayer, if you don't care about that just get the Legendary Edition.
I play it for the multiplayer. It's fun and a great time waster for 10-20 minutes. If ya want to play for the single player, better to get the legendary edition.
